A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FocusAgent research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support comparison. Some conflicting numerical reports in v2 require caution but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original WorkArena and WebArena experiments, prompt-injection evaluations, and retrieval-prompt and observation-formatting ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original navigation and security experiments, including additional model comparisons, goal-drift attacks, failure analyses, and measured latency.

M1.justification: The two-stage procedure—selecting numbered AxTree lines with an LLM and predicting actions from the pruned observation—is retained. Default soft retrieval without history and the DefenseFocusAgent prompt are unchanged. Additional model configurations and attack-generation procedures expand evaluation without revising the agent algorithm.

E1.justification: WorkArena L1 and the 381-task WebArena coverage remain unchanged. v2 adds similar-goal diversion attacks on the existing 114-task Reddit security subset, creating a bounded new adversarial scenario in which banners substitute a related task goal for the legitimate goal.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces v1's text-embedding-3-small comparator with text-embedding-3-large and Qwen3-Embedding-8B comparisons. Table 3 also adds DefenseGenericAgent, a warning-only security baseline, alongside the retained regular and guard-based agents. These materially expand the retrieval and defense comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen backbone/retriever configurations and evaluates 200- and 400-token retrieval chunks with 2000/4000-token observation caps; v1 reported the selected 200-token configuration after describing a different candidate-size sweep. It introduces input-token cost accounting, a sequential 33-task latency evaluation, and template-based goal-drift attack construction. The principal benchmark splits and step limits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds systematic analysis of tasks where GenericAgent succeeds but FocusAgent fails: 15 GPT-4.1 cases and 18 Claude cases in Appendix B. It also adds latency decomposition, explicit retrieval-budget comparisons, cost breakdowns, and goal-drift robustness testing. Existing prompt, history, formatting, and pruning-distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new latency study specifies a fixed seed and reports means, 95th percentiles, and ± dispersion, labeled 'standard deviation of the mean' in Table 11. Existing success-rate standard-error reporting and the benchmark seed counts remain unchanged; no increase in repetitions of the original experiments is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for new comparators, Qwen configurations, GPT-5-mini on WebArena, costs, latency, and goal-drift attacks; the latter report 0.9% ASR and 47.4% TSR for GPT-4.1 DefenseFocusAgent. Main Table 2 changes WorkArena GenericAgent-BT from 53.0% to 53.6% and its 5k variant from 41.8% to 44.5%, although Appendix Table 8 retains the old values. Some ablation scores change, and v1's Claude/GPT-5-mini retrieval result is removed. These are reported additions and revisions, not uniform same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The observation-pruning definition and Equation 1 cost break-even derivation, including the 20% threshold, are retained from v1 Appendix F in v2 Appendix H.1. The new attack-sampling pseudocode documents an evaluation procedure; it introduces no theoretical guarantee or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction qualify v1's performance-parity claim with 'modest degradation.' The conclusion similarly acknowledges degradation and restricts strong performance under attacks to 'certain types of attacks.' The central observation-pruning and security contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 develops explanations based on chunk size and retriever capability rather than only attributing conventional retrieval failures to inadequate contextual reasoning. New failure analyses identify missing navigation cues, omitted chart values, loops, and premature termination; the latency analysis identifies the additional retrieval call as a major practical limitation. Discussion also qualifies pruning's usefulness by model capability and explains model-dependent responses to security warnings. The original Appendix A and popup-blocking limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds API-call timing and retry-aggregation details, deterministic task-template sampling pseudocode, and pricing/local-deployment information. Its code pointer changes from the general AgentLab repository to a dedicated FocusAgent repository. These are targeted reproducibility additions; the existing retrieval prompts, defense prompt, and observation flags are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive comparisons with Prune4Web and Read More, Think More, positioning FocusAgent relative to programmatic DOM pruning and stronger models using richer observations. Additional references motivate goal-diversion attacks, cost-aware evaluation, and comparisons with other multi-call agent architectures. This substantially expands the research positioning beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 combines experimental setup and results within Section 4, subdivides the security section, and adds appendix contents. It edits grammar, affiliations, terminology, and citation style. Much of the existing introduction, method, ablation discussion, and appendix prose remains recognizable, so the editorial reorganization is limited despite the scientific additions.

P2.justification: Main comparison tables gain extensive rows, backbone groups, and cost columns, while new tables and plots present security, failure, latency, and cost evidence. v1 Figure 4 moves to the appendix as v2 Figure 7; the ASR-versus-TSR plot in v1 Figure 5b is removed. Typography, page width, and placement of appendix figures are extensively reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evaluation of the central efficiency and security claims through stronger retrieval comparisons, a warning-only defense control, and goal-drift testing. Cost accounting, failure analysis, and measured latency—10.1 versus 2.5 seconds per step—expose practical tradeoffs missing from v1, while performance claims become better qualified. Main/appendix score disagreements and erroneous savings annotations, such as Table 8 labeling $38.1 versus $55.6 as a 46% saving, weaken numerical reliability. Nevertheless, the gains in experimental scrutiny and transparency outweigh these reporting defects.
